findings.title: Password check bypassed when backupCode + totpCode both supplied
findings.body: Password verification is gated on `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)` while second-factor selection is gated on `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)`. An attacker who knows only the victim email and one valid backup code can send backupCode plus any dummy totpCode: the first condition is false so password is never verified, the second condition is true so only the backup code is verified. Backup codes become a single-factor login, bypassing the password. Require password verification independent of totpCode/backupCode presence.

findings.title: Go back / Lost access buttons submit login form
findings.body: TwoFactorFooter renders Buttons inside the login <form> without type="button" and only toggles twoFactorLostAccess / clears fields. A plain Button defaults to submit, so clicking Go back or Lost access also triggers form onSubmit and a credentials signIn call with partial codes. Add type="button" to non-submit footer buttons.

findings.title: Lost access / Cancel buttons submit disable form
findings.body: The Lost access toggle and Cancel buttons are inside <Form> without type="button" and without preventDefault. Clicking them will also submit handleDisable, sending password plus empty totpCode/backupCode and surfacing spurious 2fa_required/incorrect errors or unintended requests. Give them type="button".

findings.title: Throwing instead of returning 500 breaks API contract
findings.body: When CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing or secret length is invalid the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)`. In a Next.js API route this becomes an unhandled exception / HTML 500 instead of the JSON `{error}` shape the client expects (`await response.json()` will fail). Return `res.status(500).json({error: ...})` like setup.ts does. Same risk for JSON.parse/symmetricDecrypt failures on corrupted backupCodes.

findings.title: resetState leaves backup codes and secret in memory
findings.body: resetState clears password, error and step but not backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri or secret. After closing the DisplayBackupCodes step via backup-codes-close, the plaintext codes and TOTP secret remain in component state and the object URL is never revoked, so reopening or another session on the same page can re-render stale secrets. Clear those fields and revoke the object URL on close/unmount.

findings.title: No coverage for backup-code login or disable
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code login in next-auth-options, backup-code disable in the disable endpoint, and single-use nulling of codes, but the e2e only tests download/copy/close buttons and leaves an explicit TODO for login + disabling with backup codes. There is no test that a backup code logs in once and is then rejected, or that disable with a backup code works/fails correctly.
